[['', "L.L.C., 36 A.D.3d 401, 404–05 (1st Dep't 2007)", 'Court of Appeals precedent, held that unjust enrichment may be pleaded as an alternative to breach of contract where there is a bona fide dispute as to the enforceability or scope of the contract. The Court specifically held that dismissal of an unjust enrichment claim as duplicative of a contract claim at the pleading stage is premature where the parties dispute the applicability of the contract to the claims at issue. The Court reasoned that because the existence, validity, or scope of the governing contract may be called into question—through defenses such as fraud in the inducement, unconscionability, or the unenforceability of specific provisions on public policy grounds—a plaintiff is entitled to plead in the alternative to protect against the possibility that the contractual remedy may ultimately prove unavailable or inadequate. The Court noted that the proper time to address the preclusive effect of an express contract on an unjust enrichment claim is after discovery and on a motion for summary judgment, not on a CPLR § 3211 motion to dismiss.']]
